column1: # Readings of Strong numbers that no source writes: where one numbering writes for a word a number another writes otherwise,
#   which numbers count as one, and which numbers a source misplaces. Ours, measured on the corpus; each row says why.
#   Edit a row and run forge build: every product made with a list declares this file as an input.
# Columns: list, number, reads (the number it is read as; \N where the list names numbers only), reason.
#   fhl-prefix       a Hebrew prefix number the Faith Hope Love foundation writes on the Chinese Union Version, read as the
#                    number BHSA writes for the same prefix (UnionStrongNumbers)
#   lemmatised       a Greek form's own number read as its lemma's, where the Greek editions' tagging traditions disagree
#                    (GreekLemmaNumbers: the Clear Bible, Berean and Greek-witness links)
#   suppletion       a Greek number the dictionary's derivations cannot resolve: the number tried instead where the tagged
#                    number matches nothing in the verse, still measured against the verses before it is used (GreekNumberResolution)
#   counted-as       a number counted with another's in the tie-breaks of the Strong numbers per text (ChainedNumbers)
#   synonym          a number counted as one with reads, the first of its group, by the Strong numbers per text (StrongSynonyms)
#   clause-particle  a Greek conjunction or particle whose number Maxfield's ASV puts on an English content word, where it is
#   numeral          a numeral of the originals, read as its value (reads is a whole number, not a Strong number): the Strong
#                    numbers per text give a word that renders a run of numerals as one number all of them (GroupNumbers)

εἶπον, the aorist of 'say': Strong's own cross-references name G3004 and the printed editions lemmatise every form of it under λέγω
εἴδω: its entry borrows the missing tenses from G3700 and G3708; the editions keep οἶδα under G1492 and put εἶδον under ὁράω, so this fires only where G1492 itself is not in the verse
ἰδού, which the dictionary derives from G1492 and the editions tag as the imperative of ὁράω it is
ἴδε, which the dictionary derives from G1492 and the editions tag as the imperative of ὁράω it is
ὀπτάνομαι, the same paradigm; its derivation names the alternation in prose, so the vocabulary test refuses it

αὑτοῦ, the aspirated contraction the tagged edition writes; both Greek editions read αὐτοῦ and tag αὐτός (the dictionary's G1438 is what the word is, not what the page says: 30 verses of 835 bear it out)
μοῦ, an oblique case of the first person singular; Strong derived each form from its neighbour, so no chain reaches the nominative
